reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that: no redline and no comment were proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited paragraphs support the conclusion — the Section 2.1 and 2.4 grants are expressly 'nonexclusive, nontransferable' and impose no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Corio (the customer-side party we represent).

The only exclusivity-flavoured term identified (Section 2.4 restricting Commerce One from contacting Corio Customers for non-ASP licence sales) runs in our favour, which the rule's detection guidance treats as acceptable and not a deviation; the rationale correctly declines to flag it.

Exhibit D cooperation efforts are expressly 'non-binding' (p0198) and amount to soft effort obligations, not exclusive dealing — so the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer) is met, not merely the fallback.
Deterministic check ('no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains') passes, corroborating the compliance call; retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.
